what: The audit that makes 'convert all known workflows to BDD' a bounded, checkable claim. Each entry is an upstream *universe* and how this repo's BDD corpus accounts for every module in it: `ported` maps an upstream name to the BDD feature that is its decision-graph port; `search_space` names a workflow that is deliberately NOT ported, with the reason (an optimizer search-space, not a decision policy, so a BDD decision graph would have to invent the policy); `not_a_workflow` names a module that is not a workflow at all (engine / model / harness), one reason per group, so that code is named rather than quietly absent. `ported_all` means the whole universe is a 1:1 BDD port whose closure is proven by `bdd port-check`. A universe enumerates the `.py` files directly under `upstream`; set `recursive: true` when its workflows are not all in one directory (a package whose root holds gates next to a `workflows/` dir) - names are then the `/`-joined path minus the extension. `bdd scope-check` reads this file; `bdd scope-check --sources <ole-eval root>` puts it on trial against a live checkout (the listed names must equal the .py files on disk, so a new upstream module cannot be silently skipped). `enumerate: false` marks a universe whose upstream is not publicly enumerable (its names are pinned here and every ported feature is still existence-checked; `--sources` cannot list such an upstream, so it does not demand a directory for it). A universe declares its whole *package* when its workflows are not all in one directory (`recursive`). On top of the universes, `roots` declares the upstream trees the census claims to cover end to end; with `--sources`, every immediate child directory of a root that holds a `.py` must be some universe's `upstream`, and a root's own modules need a universe too (a root may contain another declared root, whose own sweep covers it - roots nest) - so a new upstream *directory* cannot appear without a universe accounting for it, not just a new file inside one already known.

roots.note: The workflow home of the qwen_vm line. Every immediate child directory that holds a `.py` must be a universe's `upstream` (app_scenarios, self_evolving, hybrid, lang, working_mem), and the root's own modules need one too (qwen_vm_root). So a new upstream directory under qwen_vm cannot appear without a universe accounting for it - the one-level generalisation of the per-universe check.

The deployment-validation tree: the deploy gate that must pass before any GPU deployment ships, plus the tier0/tier1 runners and the tier1 quality runner it drives. Every immediate child directory that holds a `.py` must be a universe's `upstream` (deploy_gate, tiers), so a new gate directory under code/eval cannot appear without a universe accounting for it.

The long-horizon trusted-state-machine package (R11 Path C): the model may only choose an action, and the executor gates that proposal before it acts. Its one decision module is ported; a new module under this root cannot appear without a universe accounting for it.

The Rust LayaModel crate and its Python bench harness. The crate's Python lives entirely under bench/ (src/ is Rust and target/ is a cargo build tree), so bench/ is the universe upstream and the crate root holds no .py of its own; a new .py directory beside bench/ would need a universe. The numeric parity gate is ported; the reference-capture and perf-measurement scripts are named.

The whole code tree of the evaluation repo - the top of the bound. Every immediate child directory that holds a `.py` is a universe's `upstream` (agentic_memory, clef-clm-bench, dflash2, distill, dllm, eval_index, inference, llama-eval, swebench) or is itself a declared coverage root (eval, longhorizon, qwen_vm, laya-tch), whose own sweep covers it: roots nest. The root's own module (the resumable uploader) has a universe too. So neither a new upstream directory nor a new module directly under code/ can appear without a universe accounting for it.

universes.kind: decision-guards (deterministic LLM-proposal guards)
universes.note: 66 deterministic guard scenarios, every one a @decision graph under bdd/workflows/ole_eval/ with its dsl/ole_eval/ spec; the closure is proven by `bdd port-check --cat ole_eval --pin bench/bdd/port_pins/ole_eval.json`.

universes.kind: mixed (one decision state-machine + a family of optimizer search-spaces + the package's own engine / model / harness modules)

search_space.workflows/anomaly_detection: optimizer search-space over (window, z_threshold, method, fill); eval_fn scores against ground truth, there is no deterministic policy to encode
search_space.workflows/c_program_runner: search-space over (program, input_value) where program is a compiled C/WASM artifact; the correct pick is data-dependent
search_space.workflows/data_cleaning: search-space over (program, input_offset) choosing a per-column C cleaning program; the program is discovered, not ruled
search_space.workflows/data_cleaning_columnar: column-level variant of data_cleaning; same search-space shape
search_space.workflows/data_cleaning_multistep: multi-step (12 cols x 2 steps) variant of data_cleaning; same search-space shape
search_space.workflows/data_cleaning_real: real-CSV variant with an LLM proposer; the proposer is the (learned) policy, so there is no fixed decision graph
search_space.workflows/label_stability: optimizer search-space over (window, similarity_threshold, consensus); no deterministic policy
search_space.workflows/outlier_detect: optimizer search-space over (window, threshold, fill); no deterministic policy
search_space.workflows/wasm_action_picker: search-space over (action, window, threshold, low, high); the action is looked up in a shared registry and the correct pick is data-dependent

not_a_workflow.reason: the LLM-as-optimizer engine: the propose -> evaluate -> accept loop, its state / registry plumbing, its entry points, and the training of the proposal policy. They *run* a workflow; they are not one, and the pick the loop makes is a learned / bandit proposal, not a decision graph.

the learned proposer / calibrated head: an LLM or a risk model that *supplies* the answer. The decision is theirs (weights, prompts), so a BDD graph would have to invent it - what this corpus ports is the deterministic consumer of their output (workflows/agent_permission takes the risk band as a field).

harness: benchmark runners, dataset export / bake, the hold-out auditor, the continuing-decision-stream simulator, the computer-use demo, the browser agent that drives it, and the WASM action registry / executor bridge the loop uses. They measure or feed the loop; none decides.

the browser-aware *variant* of the ported agent_permission decision graph: same gate class, same state machine, same verdict vocabulary and thresholds (risk >= 0.5 -> BLOCK, confidence < 0.6 -> ESCALATE). It only swaps in browser-specific risk *features* for the model that supplies the risk band - driven against the port it agrees on the verdict of every expressible walk (17/17); it differs only in one presentational fold, materialising a walk-stopping refusal as a terminal `refused` node where the upstream leaves the state unchanged. It is not a second decision graph, so there is no separate policy to port; the walk-shape difference is recorded, not hidden.

universes.note: The package is the upstream, not just its `workflows/` dir: `browser_gate.py` sits at the root and is a decision gate of exactly the same kind as `workflows/agent_permission.py`. Enumerating only the subdirectory left every root-level module outside the bound, so a new one there was silently unaccounted. `workflows/agent_permission` is a permission state-machine + calibrated risk gate, so it IS a decision graph and was ported (P79); the other nine `workflows/*` are parameter search-spaces for the optimizer loop; the rest of the package is named in `not_a_workflow` groups (engine / model / harness), one reason per group.

universes.upstream: agent-toolbox repo (skills/ + code/scripts/ + .githooks/; private - a set of shell/Python ops scripts, not a public workflow directory)
universes.note: The agent-toolbox decision workflows were ported to DSL first (dsl/agents/, whose README maps each spec to its upstream ops script) and then to BDD (@decision). Their upstream is a private repo of shell/Python scripts, so it cannot be enumerated publicly; the upstream names are pinned here and every ported feature must exist and be a @decision graph. `enumerate: false` tells `--sources` not to demand a directory - there is no public one to list - so the universe is accounted for by name instead of being silently omitted from the bound.

universes.kind: the package root's stray module (a bench harness)

not_a_workflow.reason: harness: the multilingual 100%-syntax bench (34 languages x prompts, driven through the lark grammars and the official compilers). It *measures* a model; it is not a workflow.

universes.note: The one module that sits directly under code/qwen_vm. A universe whose `upstream` is the root is what lets the coverage-root sweep name the root's own modules instead of leaving them unclaimed.

universes.kind: mixed (the hybrid forward-pass loop + its router pair + its ablation harness)

not_a_workflow.reason: the hybrid forward-pass engine: the continuous decode loop, the LLM<->VM bridge, the state bridge to working_mem, the WASM executor wrapper, the real-model adapter and the two demos. They *run* a loop; they are not a decision over a model proposal.

the router pair: `mode_router` is a deterministic 2-state token switch (lang vs exec, driven by the literal `<exec>` / `</exec>` markers) and `learned_router` is its learned replacement. A mode router steers one decode step - it has no model proposal to gate and no verdict vocabulary - and the learned variant *is* the model, so neither is a decision graph.
the ablation harness: the three state-tracking baselines and their real-LLM runner. They measure the loop; they decide nothing.

universes.note: The hybrid forward pass of the Percepta line: one LLM plus a deterministic router, a WASM executor and working memory. Every module here is engine / router / harness, so the universe is entirely `not_a_workflow`; the `test_*.py` files are skipped by the recursive enumeration.

universes.kind: grammar library

not_a_workflow.reason: the multilingual lark grammars + the official-compiler validators + the brace-depth truncation guidance + the lark-constrained generation helper. It is a parsing/validation library, not a decision over a model proposal.

universes.note: The grammar library the multilingual bench and the Transformer-VM line share.

universes.kind: mixed (one decision guard + the three-layer memory engine + the readout-head research)

not_a_workflow.reason: the three-layer memory engine and its deterministic reference: the trace store + sliding KV + checkpoint manager, the hot/warm/cold tiering, the core-state schema, the long-horizon simulator, the Phase-1 runner and the capacity probe.

the readout-head research: the residual-slot probe and the field / per-field / field-token-pool / dedicated readout trainers. They *train a head* - the head is the model, and its output is a proposal the corpus would gate, not the gate itself.
the package's own self-test module. It is named `tests` (not `test_*.py`), so the recursive enumeration does not skip it.

universes.note: Working memory of the long-horizon line (F3/F5/F6): the store, the tiering and the readout heads, plus the one proposal guard - `reliable_reader` is ported as a `@decision` graph (`bdd/workflows/guards/reliable_state_reader.feature`), which resolves P221's flagged borderline call. `test_reliable_reader.py` is the upstream reference and is skipped by the recursive enumeration.

universes.kind: the deployment validation gate + its tier1 quality runner

not_a_workflow.reason: the tier1 quality runner: it asks a fixed corpus and computes a pass_rate and a deterministic golden match. It *measures*; the gate decides. Its outputs are exactly the `quality` check's observable input, folded into that check's pass/fail in the port.

universes.note: The gate that must pass before any GPU deployment ships. Its verdict -- all five checks pass, else the first failing check in the gate's own order (smoke, config, quality, perf, lmcache) -- is a @decision graph (bdd/workflows/guards/deploy_gate.feature). The thresholds that turn a measurement into each check's pass/fail live in code/eval/deploy_gate/thresholds.json and belong to the harness, so they are folded into the check outcome.

universes.kind: the tier0 (smoke) and tier1 (quality) eval runners

not_a_workflow.reason: the tier runners: they drive a server and print PASS/FAIL over measured thresholds, wrapping the same checks the deploy gate chains. They are harnesses (a measurement), not the gate's verdict -- which is ported as deploy_gate.

universes.kind: one decision guard (the model-action gate) plus the package's own plumbing
universes.note: The model may only choose an action (run a candidate / declare done); parse_model_action decides whether that proposal is the contract shape before the executor acts. Ported as a 4-node validation walk. The executor's syntax/test/record bookkeeping is measurement and is folded into the gate's observable input, so it is not a graph of its own; the package __init__ is a re-export and is not enumerated (scope_enumerate_py skips __init__).

universes.kind: the LayaModel Rust-vs-PyTorch parity gate (ported) plus the reference-capture and perf-measurement bench family

not_a_workflow.reason: the measurement family: bench_pytorch reports the PyTorch latency baseline, compare_perf runs the two engines head-to-head, and api_parity replays each captured case through both engines and prints per-field agreement (its hard exit is a raw-probability disagreement at 1e-5; a 4-decimal rounding-boundary difference is only warned). Like the tier1 quality runner under code/eval, they measure; the numeric parity gate is parity_check.

the reference-capture scripts: ref_capture writes the PyTorch reference trace (token ids, pre-temperature logits, calibrated answers, a probe hidden state) and ref_raw_capture writes the unrounded probabilities, precisely so the rounded reference cannot hide a mismatch. They produce the data the parity gate reads; they decide nothing.

universes.note: The Rust-vs-PyTorch numeric parity gate for LayaModel: bench_parity compares the Rust forward pass against the captured PyTorch reference and gates the decision output -- the marker logits must agree to max|delta| < 1e-3. Ported as a 5-node walk: four named refusals in the wrapper's own order (bin not built, trace absent, no model dir, weights missing -> CANNOT_RUN_NO_BIN / _NO_TRACE / _NO_MODEL_DIR / _NO_WEIGHTS) and the single run's PASS/FAIL verdict. The tolerance and the marker-logit choice are applied inside the bench_parity binary, so the run's outcome is the graph's observable input. Proved against the live upstream by a 7-case drive of code/laya-tch/bench/parity_check.py (4 refusals + PASS + FAIL + exit-0-without-PASS).

universes.kind: mixed (the repo's code root: one standalone utility module)

not_a_workflow.reason: the resumable ModelScope uploader: it chunks a local model directory and uploads it over the hub API with retry. It moves bytes; it decides nothing.

universes.note: The code root itself: one standalone module beside the trees. Every other immediate child that holds a `.py` is either a universe's `upstream` or a declared coverage root (roots nest), so a new directory or file directly under code/ cannot appear without a universe accounting for it.

universes.kind: non-workflow (an HTTP service over the memory store)

not_a_workflow.reason: the agentic-memory service: an HTTP backend that serves the memory store (remember / recall / retrieve) over HTTP. It runs the store; the store's own policy lives in laya-mem, not here.

universes.note: The memory service tree. Named not-a-workflow: it serves the store, it does not decide.

universes.kind: mixed (the System-1 comparison bench: candidate adapters + servers + runners)

not_a_workflow.reason: the System-1 candidate adapters: one per published System-1 model, each a faithful re-implementation of that model's own scoring protocol (what it takes as input, what its head emits, how a score maps to an answer). They are the *subjects* of the comparison, not a decision this repo makes - the policy is the model's weights, which live outside the repo. One shared harness scores them all on one pipeline.

the serving wrappers and the measurement runners: an HTTP front for the fine-tuned Laya head, a Qwen3-8B embedding server, a soft-decider server, and the typed-decisions accuracy / throughput benches. They serve a model and measure it; no gate.

universes.note: The typed-decisions System-1 comparison: ~48 per-model adapters, two loaders, three servers and two benches. Every module is named; none is a decision graph (the candidates' policies are their external weights).

universes.kind: mixed (speculative-decoding patches + a patch-applier gate + a measurement harness)

not_a_workflow.reason: the speculative-decoding integration: the DFlash2 draft-model patches applied into sglang / vLLM site-packages (worker classes, kernels, model shims, the INT4 support set), and the draft-model packing scripts. They edit another project's source so a speculative decoder runs; there is no answer of their own to rule on.
the draft-model measurement harness: the three-path throughput benches, the HF direct-check harnesses, and the sglang launch wrapper. They measure.

gate_pending.sglang-patches/int4-support/apply_all_pa: the DFlash2 INT4 patch-set applier: it backs up and applies five source patches into sglang's site-packages and exits non-zero when any one fails to apply (`all_ok` -> `sys.exit(1)`), i.e. it gates the environment before a draft model may be launched. Gate-shaped, port pending.

universes.note: The DFlash2 draft-model work: patch files applied into another project, the draft packing scripts, the benches, and the patch-set applier - which is gate-shaped and registered as a pending port.

universes.kind: mixed (SFT/distill pipeline: generators + training loops + runners + two promotion gates)

not_a_workflow.reason: the SFT / distill data generators: one script per dataset round (handcrafted batches, programmatic generators, teacher-generated rows, DPO pair builders, the GPU2 agent generators). They synthesise training rows and self-check each row compiles; they decide nothing about a candidate.

the LoRA / SFT training loops: one script per optimisation round (r11..r30, the DPO pair trainer, the KD trainer, the FlashNext LoRA trainer, and the round's config). They train a candidate; the promotion verdict is drawn from the eval JSONs by the gates registered as pending.

the measurement runners and the data plumbing: the A/B eval scripts that write result JSON, the latency runner, the long-horizon runners, the few-shot eval, the short-bucket packer, the Python-syntax data filter (a predicate over rows, not a gate), the dataset preparer, the ngram config and the teacher client.

gate_pending.scripts/r28d_gamma_routing: the routing promotion gate: it compares routed vs baseline pass-rates on the 60x4 set and declares RECOMMENDED when routed beats the baseline (`Gate: routed > 61.25% -> RECOMMENDED`). A promote/reject verdict on a candidate. Port pending.
gate_pending.scripts/eval_longhorizon_gamma: the long-horizon A/B promotion gate: it reads two eval JSONs and computes pass-rate buckets and a promotion verdict against a pass-rate and a regression threshold. A promote/reject verdict on a candidate. Port pending.

universes.note: The SFT / distillation pipeline: the data generators, the training loops, the measurement runners, and the two promotion gates (routing and long-horizon) that are registered as pending ports.

universes.kind: non-workflow (the benchmark harness and the model sweeps)

not_a_workflow.reason: the llama-eval benchmark harness: the stage runners, the pass@1 benchmark drivers (humaneval / mbpp / bigcodebench / livecodebench / swebench / apps / taco / cruxeval and the archived eval scripts), the config loader and manager, the diagnostics probes, the opencompass config and the framework / harness plumbing. They run a benchmark and report a number.

the model sweeps: the sweep runners, the quantization scripts (AutoRound / AWQ / GPTQ / compressed-tensors conversion / MTP weights), the int8 head and embedding quantizers, the serve and probe scripts and the concurrency bench. They produce quantized variants and measure them; no gate.

universes.note: The llama-eval benchmark harness and the model sweeps. Every module named; none is a decision graph (they run benchmarks and produce quantized variants).

universes.kind: non-workflow (the SWE-bench inference runners + SFT data prep)

not_a_workflow.reason: the SWE-bench side: the inference runners (v1..v6 and the flashnext variants, one per model generation), the SFT-dataset preparer and the prototype diff-expert trainer. They run the benchmark and build training data; there is no gate.

universes.note: The SWE-bench side: one inference runner per model generation, the SFT-dataset preparer and a prototype trainer. Named not-a-workflow: they run the benchmark and build data.

universes.kind: mixed (the masked-diffusion LM + a ported coherence gate + two pass@1 runners)

not_a_workflow.reason: the masked-diffusion LM itself: the model / loss / sampling / training modules, the dataset loaders and the ModelScope ingest, and the hybrid->dense weight converter. It builds and trains the model; it decides nothing.

gate_pending.eval/eval_diffusion_coding: the diffusion-coding pass@1 runner: it samples from the diffusion LM, executes each candidate against the benchmark's unit tests in a subprocess and reports pass@1. A candidate's verdict, though the promote/reject is drawn by hand from the JSON. Verdict-adjacent; port pending.
gate_pending.eval/eval_ar_coding: the AR-coding pass@1 runner: the autoregressive counterpart of the diffusion-coding runner on the same benchmarks - it executes each candidate against the unit tests and reports pass@1. Verdict-adjacent; port pending.

universes.note: The diffusion-LM line: the model / training / conversion modules (named), the S4 coherence gate (ported this round to bdd/workflows/guards/s4_gate.feature), and the two pass@1 runners registered as pending.

universes.kind: mixed (the eval-results index + tooling + a report generator registered pending)

not_a_workflow.reason: the eval-results index and its tooling: the SQLite-backed store, the ingest and query tools, the CLI and the markdown report CLI, plus the perf benches. They store, format and measure results.

gate_pending.report_gen: the unified eval-report generator: it renders eval JSON into a standard markdown report and exits non-zero when the requested input or arguments are missing (and prints the threshold legend it calls 判定标准). Verdict-adjacent; port pending.

universes.note: The eval-results index: the store, the ingest / query / report tooling and the perf benches (named), plus the report generator, registered as a pending gate.

universes.kind: mixed (weight-reformat fixes + WCD/WLD plumbing + three deployment gates pending)

not_a_workflow.reason: the AWQ / GGUF weight-reformat fix: the conversion, dequant, key-rename and shard-repair scripts under one dated fix directory, plus the source-patch applier for the tool-call-history fix. They rewrite weights and patch a server; no policy over an answer.

the WCD / WLD optimization plumbing: the weighted-cache supervisor and library, the block-FP8 quantizer, and the weight-load daemon that prewarms page cache on demand. They schedule, quantize and prewarm.

gate_pending.fixes/sglang_toolcall_history_400_202608: the multi-turn tool-call fix verification: it runs four end-to-end checks (A-D) against the patched sglang and its proxy and exits 0 only when all pass (`Exit code 0 = all checks passed`). A gate over a fix. Port pending.
gate_pending.optimization/wld_sglang_20260823/e2e_awq: the AWQ-INT4 cold-vs-warm deployment e2e: it brings the model up cold and warm (with the weight-load daemon), measures health / load time and checks the generated content is consistent, exiting non-zero on any failure. A deployment gate. Port pending.
gate_pending.fixes/vllm_deadlock_watchdog_20260827/vl: the vLLM deadlock watchdog: it reads the server's metrics and engine log and decides whether a server that answers /health but makes no progress is deadlocked (running > 0 and generation stalled past a threshold), then restarts it. A state machine with a named verdict. Port pending.

universes.note: The inference fixes and optimization plumbing: the weight conversions and daemons (named), and the three verdict-bearing scripts - the tool-call fix verification, the cold/warm deployment e2e, and the vLLM deadlock watchdog - registered as pending gates.
